notes.decision: Page number is restored. The transcription shows '[ⲉⲡⲉ]' but this does not form a standard Coptic numeral; the editor's reference '286' indicates the manuscript page is most likely ⲥⲡⲋ̄ (= 286). Possibly the editor's '[ⲉⲡⲉ]' reflects a damaged ⲥ misread as ⲉ. I render as [ⲥ̄ⲡⲋ̄] to match the editor's page reference.

Translated as 'said' (3sg.m perfect of speech-introduction). The form ⲧⲧⲁⲭⲉ is unusual — almost certainly a scribal variant or dialectal form of standard Lyc. ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ (= ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' per glossary). Construction ⲧⲧⲁⲭⲉ ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ matches the standard Coptic ⲡⲉϫⲉ-ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ 'said the apostle' formula.

The cross sign ⳨ here is read as ϯ ('give'), yielding ⲛⲧⲁⲩϯ 'they gave'. This is required syntactically — the clause needs a verb between ⲛⲧⲁⲩ and the direct object ⲡⲓⲣⲉⲛ 'this name'. The use of ⳨ as shorthand for ϯ is attested in this manuscript tradition.

Read as ⲁⲩⲛⲁⲍⲙⲉ-ϥ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'they saved him forth' from ⲛⲁⲍⲙⲉ (= ⲛⲟⲩϩⲙ̄ 'save', cf. glossary entry ⲡⲛⲁⲍⲙⲉϥ). The ϩ for ⲍ is regular Lyc orthographic alternation. Subject = the multitudes (or aeons of light) who rescue the First Man. Alternative reading from ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'trust/believe' is grammatically less satisfying.

Manuscript ⳨ⲟⲩ rendered as ϯⲟⲩ 'five' — the standard Lyc. numeral '5' (cf. ⲡϯⲟⲩ ⲛⲱⲏⲣⲉ 'the Five Sons' in glossary). The reference is to the First Man's Five Sons (= the five light elements/storehouses) descending with him into the realm of destruction (ⲡⲧⲉⲕⲟ).
Read as ⲉⲧⲁϥⲕⲁⲁϥ 'who placed him' — relative perfect of ⲕⲱ 'place, set' with object suffix. The Lyc. ⲭ for ⲕ + vowel-doubling -ⲁⲩ- represents Sahidic ⲕⲁⲁϥ.

Read as ⲧⲁⲓ ⲇⲉ ϩⲱⲱϥ 'but this one for his part'. ⲧⲧⲉⲓ = ⲧⲁⲓ (demonstrative, here likely referring back as transitional 'but as for this'). ⲁⲉ = ⲇⲉ (Greek δέ); ϩⲱⲱϥ = reflexive intensifier 'for his part'.

Manuscript ⳨ⲛⲟⲩ ⲟⲩⲛ ⳨ rendered with ⳨ as ϯ. ϯⲛⲟⲩ = ⲧⲉⲛⲟⲩ 'now'. Final ϯ before next line's ⲭⲱ gives ϯⲭⲱ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ 'I am saying it' (1sg present). The standard discourse-introducer 'now therefore I say to you...' is well-attested in Manichaean homiletic register.
'Two in a myriad' (= 2 in 10,000) — standard Manichaean teaching about the rare elect-quality catechumens who fully attain the likeness of the First Man. ⲧⲃⲁ = 'myriad, ten thousand'.

The manuscript reads ⲁϥ⳨ ⲡⲟⲣⲡ[ⲟ]. With ⳨ as ϯ ('give'), and ⲡⲟⲣⲡⲟ as variant/error for ⲡⲟⲣⲟ 'kingship' (Lyc. for ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ; idiom ϯ ⲡⲟⲣⲟ 'give kingship' per glossary), the sense is 'he gave kingship to them'. The doubled ⲡ in ⲡⲟⲣⲡⲟ is unusual and may be scribal. Translation preserves 'kingship' as the most contextually fitting reading.
